note: Gate 2/Gate 7: no domain on file; the name denotes a B2B sales/market-entry agency-services concept and no identifiable qualifying consumer retailer is findable. B2B services hard-fail plus unverifiable = OUT.

name: Maktab
note: Stated reason (dead/no live site) is wrong. maktab.com resolves and is archive-confirmed live (Wayback 200 snapshot, Jun 2025); it is Saudi's leading office-supplies/stationery e-commerce retailer (Jeddah, 121 staff, online orders + delivery), an approved category with Saudi HQ. The current 503 is anti-bot WAF blocking, not a dead site; the required Gate-4 follow-up search found the live business, so all gates pass.

name: Printemps Doha
note: Gate 1/Gate 6: Printemps is a French department-store brand (HQ Paris); Printemps Doha is a franchised foreign-brand store in Doha Oasis (Al Mana was only the construction contractor) listed on the French printemps.com domain, not a standalone Qatar-HQ'd e-commerce entity.

name: Haier_Saudi

name: Attar United
note: Stated reason (building_materials) is a misclassification: it is actually a Jeddah luxury watch/jewelry authorized retailer (Chopard/Hublot/Graff). Outcome still holds on Gate 4: the live site is a brochure/boutique-locator with no cart/checkout and no consumer app (authorized dealers cannot sell these brands online), so no transactional digital channel.

name: Meed Trading Company
note: Stated reason (dead/no live site) is misleading: Meed is a real 229-store Saudi convenience/grocery chain (Al Mawarid Group), an approved category. But its own domains (meed.sa, meedstores.com) are dead/parked, meed-sa.shop reads as a WordPress services page, and it sells mainly via third-party apps (ToYou/Nana/Jahez); its own branded app's transactional nature and Gate-5b 50k+ scale are unconfirmable. Genuine unresolved ambiguity on its own digital channel.

name: Saudi Marts

name: TSC
